concepts.def: Repeated cycle of designing, prototyping and testing that progressively refines a product based on feedback.
Initial statement of the problem and requirements set by a client or identified through research, initiating the design process.
Set of measurable criteria a product must meet, covering function, materials, dimensions, cost and user needs.
Working or appearance model of a design used to test ideas, gather user feedback and refine specifications.
Critical review of a prototype against the specification, identifying improvements for the next iteration.
Information gathered from intended users through interviews, observation or testing, feeding decisions for iteration.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Design & Production Capabilities — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Design & Production Capabilities brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Design & Production Capabilities.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which document sets out measurable criteria a product must meet?
options: Brief
Specification
Catalogue
Bill of materials
Single linear process
Repeated cycles of refinement
No prototyping
Fixed first solution

mcqs.q: What is an iterative design process?
options: To inspect finished products.
A cyclical process where designs are repeatedly tested, evaluated, and refined.
A process used only for software.
A linear process from brief to final product.
Producing one unique item.
Producing items continuously without stopping.
Producing a specific quantity of identical items, then switching to make another batch.
A process used only for software.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a jig in manufacturing?
options: To hold the workpiece very tightly so it does not move.
To guide a tool and ensure consistent, accurate repeated operations.
To inspect finished products.
A process used only for software.
